engineering-physics--particle-in-a-box.title: particle in an infinite well
engineering-physics--particle-in-a-box.note: The boundary conditions quantise the allowed wavelengths, so only discrete energies survive.

engineering-physics--de-broglie-waveleng.title: de Broglie wavelength of an accelerated electron
engineering-physics--de-broglie-waveleng.note: The whole constant is fixed by the electron mass and charge, so the wavelength scales only as V to the minus one-half.

engineering-physics--davisson-germer-exp.title: Bragg condition applied to an electron beam
engineering-physics--davisson-germer-exp.note: The measured peak angle matches the wavelength predicted from 54 V, which is the evidence for the matter wave.

engineering-physics--schrodinger-time-in.title: separating time from the wave equation
engineering-physics--schrodinger-time-in.note: A single-frequency ansatz turns the time derivative into the constant E, leaving a spatial eigenvalue problem.

engineering-physics--population-inversio.title: why lasing needs pumping
engineering-physics--population-inversio.note: At thermal equilibrium the upper level is empty, so the populations must be driven past equality before the medium amplifies.

engineering-physics--numerical-aperture.title: acceptance cone from the critical angle
engineering-physics--numerical-aperture.note: The cone edge is the ray that arrives at the core wall exactly at the critical angle.

engineering-physics--hysteresis.title: soft vs hard magnetic materials
rows: high, tens to hundreds of kA/m
soft iron, silicon steel, Mn-Zn ferrite
engineering-physics--hysteresis.note: The loop area is the energy lost as heat per unit volume per cycle, so cores are chosen soft and permanent magnets hard.

engineering-physics--superconductivity.title: Type I and Type II superconductors
rows: one H_c, low (about 0.08 T for Pb)
quantised vortices between H_c1 and H_c2
high, above 100 T in some cuprates
engineering-physics--superconductivity.note: Above H_c1 flux enters as vortices that stay pinned to defects, so the wire keeps carrying current up to H_c2.

engineering-physics--clausius-mossotti-e.title: from polarizability to dielectric constant
engineering-physics--clausius-mossotti-e.note: The Lorentz local field adds the depolarising field of the surrounding dipoles, which is where the εr + 2 term comes from.
